note: Flashcard bank for AWS Study Hub. Each card: id, cert (or GENERAL), topic, front, back. Contributions welcome via PR.

cards.front: Default port for SSH
cards.back: 22 (TCP)

cards.front: Default port for HTTPS
Default port for HTTP
cards.back: 80 (TCP)

cards.front: Default port for RDP (Windows remote desktop)
Default port for DNS
cards.back: 53 (UDP and TCP)

cards.front: Default port for MySQL / Aurora MySQL
Default port for PostgreSQL
Default port for NFS (used by Amazon EFS)
How many total IPs in a /24 CIDR block? How many usable in an AWS subnet?
cards.back: 256 total; 251 usable (AWS reserves 5 per subnet).

cards.front: Formula for total IPs in a CIDR block
Why does an AWS subnet have 5 fewer usable IPs than the CIDR total?
cards.back: AWS reserves the network address, VPC router, DNS, a future-use address, and the broadcast address.

cards.front: Security Group vs Network ACL: stateful or stateless?
cards.back: Security Group = stateful (return traffic auto-allowed). Network ACL = stateless (must allow both directions).

cards.front: OSI layer of ALB vs NLB vs GLB
cards.back: ALB = Layer 7. NLB = Layer 4. GLB = Layer 3.

cards.front: IAM policy evaluation: what always wins?
cards.back: An explicit Deny always overrides any Allow. Default is implicit deny.

cards.front: IP address of the EC2 Instance Metadata Service (IMDS)
cards.back: 169.254.169.254 (link-local). Prefer IMDSv2 (token-based).

cards.front: Maximum Lambda function timeout
cards.back: 15 minutes.

cards.front: Lambda memory range
cards.back: 128 MB to 10,240 MB (10 GB). CPU scales with memory.

cards.front: Name the six Well-Architected Framework pillars
cards.back: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability.

cards.front: Which support plan includes a Technical Account Manager (TAM)?
cards.back: Enterprise (and Enterprise On-Ramp has a pooled TAM).

cards.front: Shared Responsibility Model in one line
cards.back: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud (hardware, managed service internals); the customer is responsible for security IN the cloud (data, IAM, config).

cards.front: Spot vs Reserved vs Savings Plans, in a nutshell
cards.back: Spot = deep discount for interruptible work. Reserved = commit to instance type/term. Savings Plans = commit to $/hour spend, more flexible.

cards.front: What does AWS Organizations provide?
cards.back: Consolidated billing and Service Control Policies (SCPs) across multiple accounts/OUs.

cards.front: When to use S3 Standard-IA vs Glacier?
cards.back: Standard-IA: infrequent access but millisecond retrieval. Glacier: archival with retrieval delays (much cheaper storage).

cards.front: RDS Multi-AZ vs Read Replicas
cards.back: Multi-AZ = HA/failover (standby not readable). Read Replicas = scale reads (can be promoted).

cards.front: Restrict an S3 bucket so only CloudFront can read it
cards.back: Use Origin Access Control (OAC), which updates the bucket policy to allow only the CloudFront service principal.

cards.front: Give private subnet instances outbound internet without inbound access
cards.back: NAT Gateway in a public subnet (outbound only). For IPv6, use an Egress-Only Internet Gateway.

cards.front: Decouple a producer and worker fleet that scales with load
cards.back: Put work in an SQS queue; scale workers on queue depth (ApproximateNumberOfMessages).

cards.front: Lambda invocation types
cards.back: Synchronous (API Gateway), Asynchronous (S3, SNS - retries 2x, DLQ), Poll-based/event source mapping (SQS, Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams).

cards.front: How to get microsecond reads on DynamoDB?
cards.back: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX), an in-memory write-through cache.

cards.front: GSI vs LSI
cards.back: GSI: different partition key, added anytime, eventual consistency. LSI: same partition key/different sort key, must be created at table creation.

cards.front: Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store
cards.back: Secrets Manager: built-in rotation, native RDS integration ($/secret). Parameter Store: free standard tier, SecureString via KMS, no built-in rotation.

cards.front: Cognito User Pool vs Identity Pool
cards.back: User Pool = sign-in/user directory (issues tokens). Identity Pool = exchanges identity for temporary AWS credentials via IAM roles.

cards.front: Shell access to private EC2 with no port 22 or bastion
cards.back: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager (IAM-controlled, logged to CloudWatch/S3).

cards.front: How to get EC2 memory and disk metrics into CloudWatch
cards.back: Install the CloudWatch agent; these guest-OS metrics are not published by default.

cards.front: Automate scheduled OS patching with compliance reporting
cards.back: SSM Patch Manager with maintenance windows and patch baselines.

cards.front: Service that analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs for threats
cards.back: Amazon GuardDuty.

cards.front: Service that discovers and classifies PII in S3
cards.back: Amazon Macie.

cards.front: Block SQLi/XSS at Layer 7 in front of ALB/CloudFront/API Gateway
cards.back: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall).

cards.front: Connect many VPCs + on-prem with transitive routing
cards.back: AWS Transit Gateway (hub-and-spoke). VPC Peering is non-transitive.

cards.front: What is 'Rehost' in the 7 Rs of migration?
cards.back: Lift-and-shift: move as-is with minimal change (often via AWS Application Migration Service).

cards.front: Order the 4 DR strategies by RTO (slowest to fastest)
cards.back: Backup & Restore > Pilot Light > Warm Standby > Multi-Region Active-Active.

cards.front: Deployment strategy with zero downtime and instant rollback
cards.back: Blue/green: run new version beside old, shift traffic after health checks pass.

cards.front: Detect manual changes to CloudFormation-managed resources
cards.back: CloudFormation drift detection.

cards.front: Dedicated private link to AWS with consistent bandwidth
cards.back: AWS Direct Connect (not over the public internet).

cards.front: Expose a service privately across VPCs with overlapping CIDRs
cards.back: AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoint / endpoint service).

cards.front: Answer from private docs without retraining the model
cards.back: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG): retrieve relevant docs and add them to the prompt as context.

cards.front: Single-API access to multiple foundation models on AWS
cards.back: Amazon Bedrock.

cards.front: Bedrock feature that blocks harmful content / restricts topics
cards.back: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock.

cards.front: Serverless SQL directly over S3, pay per data scanned
cards.back: Amazon Athena. Reduce cost with partitioning + Parquet (columnar).

cards.front: Serverless ETL with crawlers, Data Catalog, and Spark jobs
cards.back: AWS Glue.

cards.front: SageMaker feature for automatic hyperparameter optimization
cards.back: SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning.

cards.front: Detect model/data drift in production
cards.back: SageMaker Model Monitor.

cards.front: Let a foundation model call tools/APIs for multi-step tasks
cards.back: Amazon Bedrock Agents.

cards.front: Effect of lowering the temperature parameter
cards.back: More deterministic, focused output (less randomness/creativity).
